'''Christopher Spencer Foote''' (June 5, 1935 &ndash; June 13, 2005) was a professor of chemistry at [[UCLA]] and an expert in reactive oxygen species, in particular, [[singlet oxygen]].<ref>Greer, A.  "Christopher Foote's Discovery of the Role of [[Singlet oxygen|Singlet Oxygen]] (<sup>1</sup>O<sub>2</sub>, <sup>1</sup>Δ<sub>g</sub>) in Photosensitized Oxidation Reactions", ''Accounts of Chemical Research'' '''2006''', ''39'', 797-804</ref> He published over 250 research articles and has an [[h-index]] of 67.<ref>[[ISI Science Citation Index]] citation report excluding meeting abstracts and corrections.  Accessed Feb 2, 2009.</ref>  He was also known for his textbook ''Organic Chemistry'' (with Brown and Iverson).<ref name="anie">{{citation
 | last1 = Jensen | first1 = Frank
 | last2 = Ogilby | first2 = Peter R.
 | doi = 10.1002/anie.200502934
 | issue = 39
 | journal = Angewandte Chemie International Edition
 | page = 6268
 | title = Christopher S. Foote (1935-2005): Singlet Oxygen
 | volume = 44
 | year = 2005| doi-access = free
 }}.</ref><ref>[http://www.chem.ucla.edu/news/C_S_Foote_obituary.htm UCLA Chemist Christopher Spencer Foote Died at Age 70], UCLA Chemistry Department.</ref>

The [[American Chemical Society]] gave him their Baekeland award in 1975, named him a [[Arthur C. Cope Scholar Award|Cope Scholar]] in 1994, and gave him the [[Tolman Award]] in 1995. In 2000 an international symposium in honor of his 65th birthday was held in Hawaii.<ref>[http://www.chem.ucla.edu/research/org/HAWAII/hawaii.html Photos from Foote symposium.] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070609130705/http://www.chem.ucla.edu/research/org/HAWAII/hawaii.html |date=2007-06-09 }}</ref> The Christopher S. Foote Chair of chemistry at UCLA, currently held by [[Neil Garg]], is named after him.

==Education==
*B.S. [[Yale University]] (1957)
*Ph.D. [[Harvard University]], Organic Chemistry, (1962)<br>Research advisor, [[Robert Burns Woodward|R.B. Woodward]], "Angle strain and solvolytic reactivity in bridged bicyclic systems."<ref>Harvard HOLLIS search, author: Christopher Spencer Foote, Thesis (Ph. D.)--Harvard University, 1962.</ref>

==Research and Teaching Appointments==
*Assistant Professor, [[University of California, Los Angeles]], 1962–1969
*Professor, [[University of California, Los Angeles]], 1969–2005
